checks.outputAndTies: Return a rectangle of letters with the largest possible area such that every row, read left to right, and every column, read top to bottom, is a dictionary word. checks.actualAlgorithm: Keep the cheapest earlier price and the best profit so far. Evaluate selling at the current price before updating the minimum, so a purchase used for that sale comes from an earlier day. Start the best profit at zero to allow making no trade.
checks.correctness: For each possible sale day, buying at the smallest earlier price maximizes that day’s profit. The stored minimum contains exactly those earlier prices when the sale is evaluated. Maximizing these best-per-sale profits therefore considers the optimal legal pair implicitly. The zero initial profit wins whenever every possible trade loses money, matching the at-most-one-trade contract.
checks.workedTrace: For [5,1,4,2,7], the minimum before a sale on the final day is 1. Earlier best profits progress from 0 to 3 (buy at 1, sell at 4); the final price 7 improves that to 6. Return 6, from the purchase at index 1 and sale at index 4.
checks.edgeCases: Empty and singleton arrays return zero. Declining or equal prices return zero because no trade is required. A minimum on the final day cannot fund an earlier sale.
checks.timeDerivation: O(n+1): one pass, with constant work per price.
checks.spaceDerivation: O(1): only the running minimum and best profit are stored.

checks.actualAlgorithm: Fill a reservoir with the first k entries. For the entry at zero-based index i, choose a random position among i+1 possibilities and replace a reservoir slot only when that position is below k. This preserves equal probability for every k-element subset.
checks.correctness: After t entries, every k-subset has probability 1/C(t,k). Initially t=k and there is only one subset. At the next entry, an old subset survives when no slot is replaced, with probability (t+1−k)/(t+1). A desired subset containing the new entry has t+1−k possible predecessor subsets; each selects the slot of its one extra old entry with probability 1/(t+1). Both cases therefore have probability 1/C(t+1,k), proving uniformity of complete subsets, not merely equal individual inclusion probabilities.
checks.workedTrace: For stream [4,7,9] and k=2, begin with [4,7]. On seeing 9, a uniform draw among 0,1,2 replaces slot 0, replaces slot 1 or leaves the reservoir unchanged. The three resulting subsets are equally likely. JSON arguments are [stream,k]. C++ receives begin/end iterators; Java/Python receive one iterator; C#/JavaScript receive a list. Observed true is distribution validation, not a returned sample.
checks.edgeCases: A zero-capacity reservoir stays empty. Sampling the full stream retains every entry. Each stream position is considered once, without replacement.
checks.timeDerivation: O(n). Every stream entry is inspected once and only k sample entries are retained.
checks.spaceDerivation: O(k). The reservoir holds k values plus counters; stream input storage is not counted as auxiliary.

C++ receives begin/end iterators; Java/Python receive one iterator; C#/JavaScript receive a list. Observed true is distribution validation, not a returned sample.

checks.actualAlgorithm: Compare corresponding nodes across the mirror: left with right, then right with left. Both missing nodes match; one missing node or unequal values break symmetry.
checks.correctness: Two subtrees are mirrors exactly when both are empty, or their roots match and each left subtree mirrors the other right subtree. The recursion checks this definition at every paired position, proving both value and shape symmetry.
checks.workedTrace: For [6,3,3,1,5,5,1], the two 3 roots agree. The outer leaves match 1 with 1 and the inner leaves match 5 with 5, so the complete tree is symmetric. The walkthroughCase uses the judge’s JSON input format and expected observation.

checks.actualAlgorithm: Breadth-first search visits reachable white cells once and records each predecessor. On reaching the destination, follow predecessors back to the start and reverse the path. The input maze is unchanged.
checks.correctness: Every queued cell is an in-bounds white cell reachable from start through its recorded predecessor chain. Adding a previously unseen orthogonal white neighbor preserves this property and ensures each cell is queued once. Reaching end reconstructs a valid endpoint-inclusive path. If the queue empties, every reachable white cell has been explored, so no path exists.
checks.workedTrace: For maze [[0,0,1],[1,0,0],[0,0,0]], start (0,0) and end (2,2), BFS can discover (0,0)→(0,1)→(1,1)→(2,1)→(2,2). Every step is orthogonal and every visited cell is white, so return that path; the judge validates it as true. JSON arguments are [maze,[startRow,startColumn],[endRow,endColumn]]. Observed true means a valid path was accepted; observed false for distinct unreachable endpoints corresponds to an empty returned path. The wrapper also observes true for any empty result when start=end, a weaker check than the callable’s path contract.

checks.actualAlgorithm: Breadth-first search the starting cell’s same-color component. Flip a cell when it is enqueued so it cannot be enqueued twice, and explore only horizontal and vertical neighbors of its original color.
checks.correctness: Only cells matching the starting original color are enqueued, and each is flipped before enqueuing. That flip marks it visited, so no cell is processed twice. Four-neighbor expansion reaches exactly the starting component and changes no differently colored or disconnected cell.
checks.workedTrace: For start (0,0) in [[1,1,0],[0,1,0],[1,0,0]], the connected 1 cells are (0,0),(0,1),(1,1). Flipping them gives [[0,0,0],[0,0,0],[1,0,0]]; the isolated 1 at (2,0) remains. JSON arguments are [row,column,image], not [image,row,column]. The observed output is the mutated image; native Boolean image types are converted by their wrappers.
checks.edgeCases: Diagonal contact alone does not connect cells. An isolated starting pixel is still flipped. The starting value determines the component before any recoloring.
checks.timeDerivation: O(rows × columns). Each component cell is flipped before enqueueing and considers four neighbors, preventing duplicate enqueues.
checks.spaceDerivation: O(rows × columns). The queue contains cells from the component; JavaScript retains its consumed queue entries until the call ends.

checks.actualAlgorithm: Repeatedly remove vertices with no incoming edges. An acyclic directed graph eventually loses every vertex. If vertices remain, each has an incoming edge within the remainder, which implies a directed cycle.
checks.correctness: Removing an indegree-zero vertex cannot remove a directed cycle, since each cycle vertex has an incoming cycle edge. A DAG always has an indegree-zero vertex in every nonempty remainder. Thus all vertices are removed exactly when no directed cycle exists.
checks.workedTrace: For edges 0→1, 1→2 and 2→0, every vertex has indegree one. The initial ready queue is empty, so none of the three vertices can be removed and the answer is true.
checks.edgeCases: A self-loop is a cycle. All disconnected components must be considered. Duplicate edges increment and decrement indegrees consistently.
checks.timeDerivation: O(V+E) Each vertex is processed once and each edge is examined once.
checks.spaceDerivation: O(V+E) Visited state and pending/recursive vertices are bounded by V; constructing adjacency additionally stores E edges.

Recreating every outgoing edge through the map preserves edge multiplicity, cycles and shared neighbors without using an original node in the returned graph.
checks.workedTrace: Use vertices 0,1,2 with edges 0→2 twice, 2→1 and 1→0. Create copy 0, then copy 2 and append it twice to copy 0. JSON arguments [vertexCount, directedEdgePairs] construct a graph rooted at vertex 0. The callable returns the copied root; expected true records structural validation, not a boolean return.
checks.edgeCases: Cycles and self-loops must terminate through the identity map. Duplicate edges must remain duplicated. Equal labels alone do not prove a deep copy; the judge checks node identity. Only vertices reachable from the supplied starting vertex belong in its clone.
checks.timeDerivation: O(V + E) time over the reachable graph. Each reachable vertex is enqueued once and each outgoing edge is copied once.
checks.spaceDerivation: O(V) auxiliary space, plus O(V + E) for the returned graph. The identity map and queue store V vertices; returned adjacency stores E edges.

Duplicate edges and cycles must be preserved. Allocate new vertices and edges for the reachable component. Preserve original labels/edges and object separation, cycles and shared targets. checks.workedTrace: For edges 0−1−2−3−0 and isolated vertex 4, color {0,2,4} one color and {1,3} the other. Every edge crosses colors, so all 5 vertices can be placed.
checks.edgeCases: Disconnected and isolated vertices must all be processed. A self-loop cannot connect opposite groups. An odd cycle fails; an even cycle does not.

checks.actualAlgorithm: Breadth-first search the implicit graph of dictionary words differing at one position. Generate each lowercase substitution and remove a word from the unvisited set when enqueuing it, so the first reached target has minimum distance. The dictionary input is not modified.
checks.correctness: Every generated neighbor differs from the current word by exactly one permitted lowercase substitution and belongs to the unvisited dictionary. Breadth-first search processes words in nondecreasing path length. Marking a word visited when enqueued prevents redundant paths without losing a shorter route. Therefore the first target reached has minimum substitution count; exhausting the queue proves no permitted transformation exists.
checks.workedTrace: Use dictionary {bike, bile, tile, tide}, source bake and target tide. The BFS reaches bike at distance 1, bile at 2, tile at 3, and tide at 4. Each step changes exactly one character: bake → bike → bile → tile → tide. No earlier layer reaches tide, so return 4.
checks.edgeCases: Identical source and target return 0 even before searching the dictionary. Missing dictionary connections return -1. The source need not be a dictionary member; generated intermediate and target words must belong to the dictionary.
checks.timeDerivation: O(M + 26 V L squared) expected time for M dictionary entries, V visited words and word length L, including candidate creation and hashing. Each visited word tries 26 letters at L positions; creating and hashing a candidate costs O(L).
checks.spaceDerivation: O(M + V L) auxiliary space for copied dictionary references and BFS candidate strings. Dictionary membership state and queued candidate strings dominate storage.

checks.correctness: Topological processing removes a vertex only after every incoming edge has been considered. Its stored length is therefore the greatest path length ending there. Relaxing each outgoing edge extends exactly those paths by one vertex, and every DAG path is represented by such extensions.

checks.edgeCases: A path counts vertices rather than edges. Disconnected components must all be considered. The graph is acyclic.

checks.spaceDerivation: O(vertices + edges) Memoized path lengths require V entries; DFS or the ready queue holds at most V vertices.

checks.actualAlgorithm: Take as many of each denomination as possible, largest first. For this fixed US coin system the greedy choices are optimal; the remainder is then solved with smaller coins.
checks.correctness: Normalize any coin representation without increasing its count: replace five pennies by a nickel, two nickels by a dime, three dimes by a quarter and nickel, and two dimes plus a nickel by a quarter. After these exchanges, pennies are fewer than five, nickels fewer than two, and the total below a quarter is at most 24. Replace two quarters by a half-dollar and two half-dollars by a dollar. The normalized smaller-coin remainder is then below each larger denomination. Its counts must therefore equal successive greedy quotients and remainders, proving that greedy uses no more coins than any representation.
checks.workedTrace: For 76 cents, take one 50-cent coin, then one 25-cent coin, then one penny. This uses 3 coins; the remainders are 26, 1 and 0.
checks.edgeCases: Zero cents needs zero coins. The proof depends on these fixed US denominations. A large amount is handled by division, not one iteration per coin.
checks.timeDerivation: O(1), six denominations Exactly six quotient/remainder steps are performed, independent of the number of coins returned.
checks.spaceDerivation: O(1) Only the fixed denomination list and a remainder/count are retained.

checks.actualAlgorithm: Take as many of each denomination as possible, largest first. For this fixed US coin system the greedy choices are optimal; the remainder is then solved with smaller coins.
checks.correctness: Normalize any coin representation without increasing its count: replace five pennies by a nickel, two nickels by a dime, three dimes by a quarter and nickel, and two dimes plus a nickel by a quarter. After these exchanges, pennies are fewer than five, nickels fewer than two, and the total below a quarter is at most 24. Replace two quarters by a half-dollar and two half-dollars by a dollar. The normalized smaller-coin remainder is then below each larger denomination. Its counts must therefore equal successive greedy quotients and remainders, proving that greedy uses no more coins than any representation.

checks.actualAlgorithm: Sort durations and pair opposite ends. Pairing the largest duration with the smallest available one minimizes the possible maximum pair sum by the exchange argument, and yields the required canonical order.
checks.correctness: Let the smallest remaining duration be s and the largest be M. If an assignment pairs M with x and s with y, replacing those pairs with (M, s) and (x, y) cannot increase the previous maximum pair sum: M + s ≤ M + x and x + y ≤ x + M. Thus an optimum exists containing the extreme pair. Repeating the argument proves the sorted opposite-end pairing is optimal and gives the required canonical order.
checks.workedTrace: Sort durations [12, 3, 8, 5, 17, 9] into [3, 5, 8, 9, 12, 17]. Pair opposite ends: (3, 17), (5, 12), (8, 9). Their sums are 20, 17 and 17. Return [[3, 17], [5, 12], [8, 9]], whose maximum pair sum is 20.
checks.edgeCases: The number of durations is even. Equal durations remain separate tasks and may create identical pairs. Two tasks make one pair; zero tasks make an empty result.
checks.timeDerivation: O(n log n) time. Sorting dominates the n/2 constant-time pair constructions.
checks.spaceDerivation: O(n) space for the sorted copy and returned pairs. The output contains n/2 pairs; C#/JavaScript and C++ also hold an O(n) sorted copy.

checks.actualAlgorithm: Sort closed intervals by their right endpoints. When the most recent chosen point does not cover the next interval, choose that interval’s right endpoint; this also reaches as far right as possible for later intervals.
checks.correctness: For the unhit interval with earliest right endpoint, every feasible cover must choose some point inside it. Moving that point to its right endpoint cannot uncover any later-ending interval it previously hit. Thus selecting that endpoint is safe, and repeating on remaining unhit intervals yields a minimum cover.
checks.workedTrace: For closed intervals [1,2], [2,5] and [6,9], choose point 2 for the first interval; it also hits the second at its endpoint. Point 9 hits the third, giving 2 visits.

checks.actualAlgorithm: Sort the values. For each possible first value, run a two-pointer sum search over the entire array. The pointers may coincide and the first value remains eligible, matching this EPI contract that permits element reuse.

checks.actualAlgorithm: Keep indices of increasing heights. When a shorter bar arrives, each removed bar determines a rectangle ending immediately before it; the stack gives its left boundary. A zero-height sentinel finishes the remaining bars.

checks.workedTrace: For heights [2,1,2], the middle bar removes the first height-2 candidate with area 2. At the final sentinel, the last height-2 bar also gives area 2, then height 1 spans all three bars and gives the answer 3.
checks.edgeCases: An empty histogram has area 0. Equal adjacent heights must still permit a rectangle spanning the full run. A zero-height bar ends every positive-height rectangle crossing it.
checks.timeDerivation: O(n) Each bar index is pushed once and popped at most once.

checks.actualAlgorithm: A dictionary locates each cache node, and a linked list tracks recency. Lookup and reinsertion move a node to the front; reinsertion deliberately preserves its old price. New entries evict the back node when capacity is reached.
checks.correctness: The dictionary and linked list contain exactly the same keys, and list order is most-recent to least-recent. Lookup and reinsertion move the located node to the front without changing its stored price. Removing the back node before a new insertion therefore evicts exactly the least-recent key; erasure removes both representations together.
checks.workedTrace: With capacity 2, insert (1,10), insert (2,20), reinsert (1,99), then insert (3,30). Key 1 still costs 10 and is recent, so key 2 is evicted. Lookups return 10, −1 and 30 for keys 1, 2 and 3. JSON arguments contain one command array. LruCache initializes capacity; lookup/erase commands include expected results (erase uses 1/0). The wrapper observes all commands succeeding as true; the class itself has separate lookup, insert and erase results.

checks.correctness: For the current word, any earlier occurrence farther left than its latest occurrence gives a no-smaller distance. checks.actualAlgorithm: Expand a sliding window while counting its required words. Once every keyword is present, advance the left edge as far as possible, recording shorter covering windows before removing each left entry.
checks.correctness: The window counts record exactly the required-word multiplicities between left and right, and present counts the keywords with positive multiplicity. Expansion makes every possible right endpoint available. While the window covers the set, shrinking examines its shortest valid suffix before removing an indispensable word. A globally optimal interval appears during the iteration at its right endpoint, so the best recorded interval is optimal.
checks.workedTrace: For [oak, cedar, ash, oak, elm, ash] and keywords {oak, ash, elm}, the window first covers everything at indices [0, 4]. Removing oak at 0 preserves another oak at 3; removing cedar at 1 loses no keyword. This reaches [2, 4], containing ash, oak, elm in three entries. Return (2, 4); the protocol checks length 3. The callable returns inclusive zero-based endpoints. The executable walkthrough expected value is their length after the wrapper validates keyword coverage.
checks.edgeCases: Duplicate occurrences in the paragraph must not count as distinct keywords. Irrelevant words at either edge can be removed. The input set determines keyword membership; a covering interval is guaranteed by this exercise.
checks.timeDerivation: O(n + k) expected time. Each window endpoint advances at most n times after O(k) initialization. The entry-count bound treats word hashing/comparison as constant; include examined character lengths when words are unbounded.
checks.spaceDerivation: O(k) auxiliary space for keyword counts. At most k keyword counts are stored.

checks.actualAlgorithm: For each distinct keyword, track the latest possible starting index of a prefix of the required sequence. A matching later keyword extends the preceding prefix. Whenever the final keyword matches, compare the resulting interval with the best seen.
checks.correctness: For each keyword position j, start[j] stores the latest starting position of a valid sequence of keywords 0 through j in the processed paragraph. The first keyword starts a new prefix; a later keyword can extend only a previously completed preceding prefix. Keeping the latest start minimizes the length for any fixed ending position. Checking every occurrence of the final keyword therefore finds a globally shortest covering interval.
checks.workedTrace: Use paragraph [elm, oak, cedar, elm, oak, ash, pine] and ordered keywords [elm, oak, ash]. The first elm/oak prefix starts at 0. The elm at index 3 replaces its start, and oak at 4 extends that newer prefix. Ash at 5 completes indices [3, 5], a three-word interval. The method returns (3, 5); the existing judge reports its length, 3. The callable returns inclusive zero-based endpoints. The executable walkthrough expected value is their length after the wrapper checks the required keyword sequence.
checks.edgeCases: Keywords are distinct and the supplied corpus guarantees a covering interval. Repeated paragraph matches must allow a newer, shorter prefix to replace an older one. A single keyword gives a one-entry interval; ties may use any shortest valid interval.

Stop a trajectory once it falls below its start, because smaller starts have already been verified; even starts immediately reduce to smaller values. A repeated value detects a nonterminating cycle. Checked arithmetic prevents silently wrapping a trajectory.

checks.edgeCases: n=1 has no nontrivial trajectory to examine. Even starts immediately reduce to smaller starts. Checked arithmetic prevents a wrapped trajectory from masquerading as convergence.

Buying extends the previous transaction count; selling completes the current one. Descending updates use the prior day’s lower-count state, so no overlapping holdings are introduced.

checks.actualAlgorithm: Track used digits for every row, column and subgrid. Repeatedly choose an empty cell with the fewest legal candidates, try each candidate, and undo failed choices. Only initially empty cells are assigned, preserving clues.
checks.correctness: The row, column and subgrid tables describe exactly the digits already placed. Every attempted candidate is absent from all three relevant tables, so each placement preserves Sudoku validity and every original clue remains untouched. Failed branches undo both the cell and its table entries. Trying every legal candidate is complete: any valid completion must choose one of them. The fewest-candidates heuristic changes only search order, not which completions are possible.

The top-left block forces 3 at (1, 0), followed by 2 at (1, 3). Continuing gives [[1, 2, 3, 4], [3, 4, 1, 2], [2, 1, 4, 3], [4, 3, 2, 1]]. Every clue is preserved and every unit is valid; the adapter returns true.
checks.edgeCases: A fully solved board requires no assignments. Subgrid width is the square root of the valid board dimension, including 4 by 4 boards. Only zero cells are changed; a dead-end branch must undo its tentative digit before trying another.
checks.timeDerivation: Exponential search: at most O(n^e) branches for e empty cells on an n by n board, with O(n³) candidate scanning per search node. Each recursive choice fills an empty cell, giving at most n choices at each of e branching levels; the local candidate-check cost multiplies that tree size.
checks.spaceDerivation: O(n² + en) auxiliary space for the used-digit tables and up to n retained candidate choices in each of e recursive frames. Each live recursive call and retained candidate structure is counted; the board itself belongs to the caller.

checks.actualAlgorithm: Map each binary counter value i to i XOR (i shifted right once). This reflected Gray-code mapping visits every bit pattern once and changes one bit between consecutive outputs.
checks.correctness: The map g(i)=i XOR (i>>1) is invertible on b-bit values, so all 2^b outputs are distinct. Consecutive binary values differ by a carry run; XORing each with its right shift cancels that run except at one bit, giving consecutive Gray values Hamming distance one. For b>0 the reflected sequence also closes cyclically: its last value is 1<<(b-1), one bit from zero. The bank adapter only requires consecutive output pairs.
checks.workedTrace: For 3 bits, i=0..7 maps to [0,1,3,2,6,7,5,4]. For example 3 XOR 2 = 1 and 2 XOR 6 = 4, each a single set bit. All eight values occur exactly once.
checks.edgeCases: Zero bits gives the single value [0]. Do not repeat a pattern or use values outside the b-bit range. The output has exponential size even though each value is computed in constant word operations.
checks.timeDerivation: O(2^b) time for b bits. Formula variants perform constant word operations per one of 2^b outputs; search variants have the separately stated branching bound.
checks.spaceDerivation: O(1) auxiliary space, plus O(2^b) output space. Formula variants retain only loop state beyond output; search retains its history and path stack.

The example true reports structural validation; implement the displayed sequence/mutation API, not a function returning true.

checks.actualAlgorithm: Search the b-dimensional bit cube from zero. Try flipping each bit of the last code; append only an unseen result and backtrack if it cannot complete the sequence. At full length, also test that the last and first code differ by one bit.
checks.correctness: The history set equals the current path and prevents repeated codes. Every extension changes exactly one bit, so any full path has all 2^b distinct b-bit values with valid neighbors. The final check additionally closes the cycle. Trying every unused one-bit neighbor is complete for this search. For b>0 the reflected sequence also closes cyclically: its last value is 1<<(b-1), one bit from zero. The bank adapter only requires consecutive output pairs.

checks.edgeCases: Zero bits gives the single value [0]. Do not repeat a pattern or use values outside the b-bit range. The output has exponential size even though each value is computed in constant word operations.
checks.timeDerivation: O(b·b^(2^b)) conservative backtracking bound: depth is at most 2^b, each node tries b bit flips and set operations. The observed first successful path is often much shorter; a direct-formula linear bound does not describe this implementation. Formula variants perform constant word operations per one of 2^b outputs; search variants have the separately stated branching bound.

A new value v at most covered + 1 supplies the interval v through v + covered, adjoining the old interval without a gap. If v is larger, neither it nor any later value can create covered + 1. Thus the first gap, or the first value after the final covered interval, is the smallest missing positive sum.
checks.workedTrace: Sort [1, 1, 4, 9]. The first 1 makes all sums through 1 attainable; the second extends that through 2. The next value is 4, greater than covered + 1 = 3. No subset can total 3, so return 3 without using the 9.
checks.edgeCases: Zeros do not extend the covered interval. Repeated small values can extend coverage and must not be discarded. An empty array, or an array without 1, has answer 1.

checks.actualAlgorithm: Copy intervals strictly before the new closed interval. Merge every interval whose start touches or overlaps the growing interval, then append the merged interval and untouched suffix.
checks.correctness: All intervals before the first overlap end before the new start and can be copied unchanged. While starts are no greater than the growing end, each interval joins the same closed union. The remaining suffix begins after that union and is unchanged, yielding a sorted disjoint result.
checks.workedTrace: Insert [3,8] into [[1,3],[7,10]]. The closed interval [1,3] touches the new start, producing [1,8]. That overlaps [7,10], extending the merged range to [1,10].
checks.edgeCases: Touching closed endpoints count as overlap. An insertion may merge several intervals, not just one neighbor. An empty input returns the new interval alone.
checks.timeDerivation: O(n) time. The before/overlap/after phases together consume every existing interval once.
checks.spaceDerivation: O(n) output space and O(1) other auxiliary space. The result contains at most n+1 intervals; scan indices and the growing interval need constant extra space.

Merge overlapping ranges, or touching ranges when either touching endpoint is closed. Keep a boundary closed if either contributor includes it, so the resulting intervals represent exactly the original union.

checks.actualAlgorithm: Split the list with slow/fast pointers, sort both halves recursively, then merge their original nodes. Choosing the left node on equal values preserves the relative order of ties.
checks.correctness: Splitting decreases the list size, so induction gives two sorted halves. The merge repeatedly selects the least head, preserving sorted order and every original node. On equal values it selects from the left half first. Since all left-half nodes originally preceded right-half nodes, and recursive calls preserve their internal tie order, the complete merge sort is stable.
checks.workedTrace: Label the two 7-valued nodes in [7, 3, 7, 1] as 7a and 7b. The halves sort to [3, 7a] and [1, 7b]. Merging emits 1, then 3; at the tie it takes 7a before 7b. Return values [1, 3, 7, 7], with the original equal-valued nodes still in their original order.
checks.edgeCases: Null and one-node lists are already sorted. Repeated values must preserve node order, not merely sorted values. The list is split before recursion and original nodes are relinked rather than copied.
checks.timeDerivation: O(n log n) time. Each recursion level splits/merges O(n) nodes and balanced halves give O(log n) levels.
checks.spaceDerivation: O(log n) recursion space; nodes are reused. Recursion depth is logarithmic; merging relinks existing nodes and uses only a constant-size sentinel per active merge.
checks.callableAgreement: Callable: ListNode<int>? StableSortList(ListNode<int>? L). Returns the new head of the relinked original nodes; equal nodes retain identity order. The displayed JSON output serializes node values.

checks.actualAlgorithm: Sort the salaries. Treat the smaller salaries as fully paid, and divide the remaining target equally among the remaining employees. The first candidate cap no greater than the next salary is the answer. A target above the original payroll is impossible.
checks.correctness: After fixing the i smallest salaries, paid is their unchanged total. Any cap at least those salaries contributes paid plus cap times the remaining employee count. The first candidate at most the next salary satisfies this equation in the correct piecewise-linear segment; no smaller cap reaches the target.
checks.workedTrace: For salaries [5,10,20] and target 29, a cap below 5 cannot suffice. Pay 5 unchanged, then 10 unchanged; the remaining employee must receive 29−15=14. Cap 14 gives 5+10+14=29.
checks.edgeCases: A target above the original payroll returns −1. A target equal to the original total returns the largest salary. A zero target gives cap zero for a nonempty nonnegative salary list.
checks.timeDerivation: O(n log n) time. Sorting dominates a single pass through salaries and a constant-time cap calculation per position.
checks.spaceDerivation: O(n) auxiliary space for the sorted copy. Only a prefix total and candidate cap are needed beyond sorted storage.
checks.callableAgreement: Callable: double FindSalaryCap(int target_payroll, List<int> current_salaries). Sort a copy; caller input stays unchanged.

checks.actualAlgorithm: Store each value together with the maximum of its stack prefix. Pop reveals the previous prefix maximum immediately. Initialize clears the logical stack; the underlying value-tuple stack retains its allocated capacity.
checks.correctness: Every stored pair holds its pushed value and the maximum of the prefix ending at that entry. Push computes that prefix maximum from the old top and the new value. Pop removes exactly the last prefix, exposing the correct maximum for the remaining stack. Initialize clears every pair, and Empty checks whether any prefix remains. Duplicate maxima remain represented independently.
checks.workedTrace: Initialize, push -4, push 7, and push another 7. The stored prefix maxima are -4, 7, 7. Pop one 7: Max still returns 7. Pop the second 7: Max returns -4. Pop -4: Empty becomes true. The supplied operation trace checks these results, so the stateful adapter returns true.
checks.edgeCases: Duplicate maximum values must survive until their last copy is popped. All-negative stacks must not use zero as their maximum baseline. Pop and Max require a nonempty stack; Initialize discards prior state.
checks.timeDerivation: Push is O(1) amortized, with O(p) when its backing array grows; Pop, Max, Empty and Initialize are O(1) for these value-only entries. Push computes one maximum; all queries inspect only the top pair. Backing-container growth accounts for amortization.
checks.spaceDerivation: O(p) retained space for the peak number of entries over the object lifetime, including across Initialize calls. Every stored entry holds two integers; container retention may follow peak size.

checks.actualAlgorithm: Track a head index and count in a circular array. Enqueue writes at (head+count) modulo capacity. When full, copy logical queue order into a doubled array. Dequeue advances head without shifting elements.

checks.workedTrace: With capacity 2, enqueue 11 and 22, dequeue 11, then enqueue 33: storage wraps. Enqueue 44 triggers growth while preserving logical order [22,33,44]; dequeuing returns those three values and Size becomes zero.
checks.edgeCases: Growth must preserve order after head wraparound. Initialize resets the queue. Backing capacity is retained after dequeues, so space follows peak size.
checks.timeDerivation: Enqueue: O(1) amortized; Dequeue/Size: O(1); Initialize: O(capacity) Capacity doubles, so total copied entries form a geometric series across enqueues; dequeue only advances the head.
checks.spaceDerivation: O(initial capacity + peak queue size since Initialize); the buffer does not shrink after dequeues The buffer retains its capacity after removal and is bounded by initial capacity plus peak occupancy.

checks.actualAlgorithm: Push new entries onto an incoming stack. When the outgoing stack is empty, transfer all entries to it, reversing their order so its top is the oldest queue entry. Initialize clears both stacks.
checks.correctness: Reading outgoing from top to bottom, followed by incoming from bottom to top, gives the queue’s logical FIFO order. Enqueue appends to the latter part. Transferring all incoming entries when outgoing is empty reverses them into exactly the order required for dequeues. Clearing both stacks establishes the empty-queue invariant.
checks.workedTrace: Enqueue 14 and 9. The first dequeue transfers them so 14 is removed first. Enqueue 5 while 9 remains in outgoing; dequeues then return 9 and 5. The resulting trace is FIFO even though both underlying containers are LIFO.
checks.edgeCases: Initialize discards all prior state. Interleaved enqueue/dequeue calls must not transfer into a nonempty outgoing stack. Dequeue on an empty queue is outside the valid operation sequence and throws.
checks.timeDerivation: O(1) amortized enqueue/dequeue: each entry is pushed into incoming, moved once to outgoing, and popped once. One dequeue can trigger O(n) transfer work. Reset may discard all live entries. Each entry crosses between stacks at most once between enqueue and dequeue.
checks.spaceDerivation: O(p) storage for peak live entries in the backing stacks; array-based stacks may retain allocated capacity after pops. The stacks partition live entries but may retain allocated capacity after removals.

checks.actualAlgorithm: Keep a normal FIFO queue and a decreasing deque of possible maxima. A newly enqueued value removes smaller candidates behind it; dequeue removes the front candidate only when that same value leaves. Equal maxima are retained separately.
checks.correctness: The candidate deque is nonincreasing and its first value is the queue maximum. An older candidate smaller than a newly enqueued value cannot become maximum before that newer value leaves, so discarding it is safe. Equal candidates are retained separately so removing one equal maximum does not discard the other. Dequeue removes a candidate only when its matching queue value leaves.
checks.workedTrace: Enqueue 3,8,8. The first 8 removes 3 from the candidate deque, but both 8s remain. Dequeue returns 3 and then one 8; Max still returns 8 because the second maximum is still queued. The final dequeue returns that last 8.
checks.edgeCases: Duplicate maxima must be retained until each copy leaves. Initialize clears both the FIFO queue and the candidate deque. Negative values require no special sentinel maximum. Max and Dequeue require a nonempty queue.
checks.timeDerivation: Enqueue/Dequeue are O(1) amortized: each value is inserted and removed at most once from each deque. One enqueue can remove O(n) dominated candidates. Max reads one front entry in O(1). Each candidate can be discarded only once, so repeated removal loops sum linearly across a trace.
checks.spaceDerivation: O(p) storage for peak live queue entries, including candidate values and retained backing capacity; linked/deque containers may release removed entries. FIFO values and candidate values are each bounded by live/peak occupancy according to container retention.

checks.actualAlgorithm: Enumerate all three cut positions with at most three digits per part. Keep a candidate only if each part is at most 255 and has no leading zero unless the part is exactly zero.
checks.correctness: Every valid IPv4 address partitions the digit string into four parts of lengths 1 through 3, so its three cuts appear among the enumerated choices. The validator accepts exactly nonempty parts of at most three digits, numeric value at most 255, and no forbidden leading zero. Therefore every emitted address is valid and every valid partition is emitted.

checks.actualAlgorithm: Encoding groups each maximal run and writes its decimal length followed by its character. Decoding accumulates all digits of the next length, then repeats the following nondigit character and resets the count.

Nondigit input characters make the representation unambiguous.
checks.workedTrace: For decoded text "qqqqqqqqqqqqrr", Encoding counts twelve q characters and two r characters, returning "12q2r". Decoding accumulates digits 1 then 2 into count 12, emits twelve q characters, then emits two r characters. Both directions recover the other value.

checks.actualAlgorithm: Use an unsigned rolling polynomial hash for the pattern and each equal-length text window. A matching hash triggers a full character comparison, so hash collisions cannot produce a false match. Return the first verified window.
checks.correctness: The rolling hash invariant is the polynomial hash of the current text window, using unsigned wraparound arithmetic consistently for pattern and text. Removing the outgoing weighted character, multiplying by the radix and adding the incoming character preserves that invariant. Equal hashes trigger an exact span comparison, so collisions cannot create false matches. Windows are considered from left to right, making the first verified match the required answer.
checks.workedTrace: Search text cedar-ridge for pattern ridge. The pattern has length 5. The initial window is cedar; rolling updates examine windows starting at 1 through 5 without a verified match. The window beginning at index 6 is ridge. Its hash agrees and the character comparison succeeds, so return 6.
checks.edgeCases: An empty pattern matches at index 0. A pattern longer than the text cannot match. Repeated matches return the first index; equal hashes alone never establish equality.
checks.timeDerivation: O(n + m) time when hash matches are rare; O(nm) worst-case time with repeated hash collisions, for text length n and pattern length m. KMP fallback decreases a prefix length previously increased by scans; rolling hashes cost constant time per window plus exact verification when hashes agree.
checks.spaceDerivation: O(1) auxiliary space. Prefix tables, converted strings and Java verification substrings are accounted for separately from scalar hash state.

checks.correctness: The running minimum is the cheapest price seen before or at the current selling day. Buying at that minimum maximizes profit for this selling day, and the stored best covers all processed selling days. Starting best at zero permits no transaction when every sale would lose money.

checks.actualAlgorithm: Backtrack over candidate indices in nondecreasing order. Reusing the current index permits repeated values; never moving backward prevents duplicate combinations.
checks.correctness: The path uses candidate indices in nondecreasing order, so every multiset of chosen candidates has one recursion order. Reusing the same index permits repeated copies. Each call subtracts a positive candidate, and reaching remainder zero records exactly a target-sum combination; every valid multiset follows one such branch.
checks.workedTrace: For candidates [3,4,7] and target 10, choosing 3,3,4 completes one branch. Choosing 3,7 completes another. No other candidate multiset totals 10, so return [[3,3,4],[3,7]].
checks.edgeCases: Candidates are positive and distinct, so recursive remainders strictly decrease. The public target is at least 1; zero remainder is the successful internal base case. Candidates larger than the remaining target are skipped. A candidate may be reused; changing selection order does not create a new combination.
checks.timeDerivation: O(c^(d+1) + output size) upper bound for c candidates and d = target / smallest candidate. The recursion depth is at most d=floor(target/min(candidates)); each level tries c candidates. Copying successful paths contributes the total output length.
checks.spaceDerivation: O(d) recursion and current-path space, excluding output. The active path and recursion stack each have at most d entries; saved solutions are output space.

Return each combination once, in any order. This is a value-result callable. The source-bank statement adds no general input-preservation or object-identity requirement; the ordinary function wrapper compares the serialized return value. Both the outer order and the order within each group/triple/combination are unrestricted; duplicate occurrences still matter.

Exchanging an optimal solution’s first choice with that earliest-finishing choice cannot reduce its size. Repeating this argument proves the greedy maximum retained set; removing the rest is minimal.

checks.actualAlgorithm: Track a sliding window and its largest observed character frequency. Shrink when the window length minus that frequency exceeds k. The historical maximum safely bounds the longest achievable window.
checks.correctness: With an exact frequency f, a length-w window needs w-f replacements. most never decreases: when it increases to f, the current character really occurs f times in the window. The loop retains width at most most+k, and width cannot grow while most is stale after shrinking: the previous width was already most+k. Consequently each newly recorded larger width is witnessed while the count supplying most is present, and is feasible. Stale counts may retain an infeasible window of an already-achieved width, but cannot inflate best. A complete path whose highest node is the current node may use both child gains. Considering that complete path at every node covers every possible nonempty simple tree path.
checks.workedTrace: For [-5,4,7,2,3,null,6], the left gain into root -5 is 4+3=7 and the right gain is 7+6=13. Joining them through the root yields 7-5+13=15, realized by 3→4→-5→7→6. Return 15.

checks.actualAlgorithm: Group files by size and a fingerprint of at most 64 bytes each at the beginning, middle and end. For each matching pair, orient the paths by modification time.
checks.correctness: Equal fingerprints identify exactly the candidate groups defined by the adapter. Traversing every directory visits each file, and grouping retains enough information to emit each pair once without a full-content scan.
checks.workedTrace: The controlled directory contains a.txt and nested/b.txt, both with the bytes "same bytes". Their sizes and all three bounded samples match. Their modification times are 1000 and 2000, so report their full paths with a.txt first as the earlier-time candidate. This orientation is a heuristic, and equal fingerprints can still be false positives; neither file is changed. JSON supplies controlled file descriptors. The callable receives the temporary directory’s full path and returns FilePaths pairs containing full paths; displayed expected paths are relative to that directory.

checks.actualAlgorithm: Push new items to an input stack. When the output stack is empty, transfer all input items into it; this reverses their order once.
checks.correctness: The output stack top is always the oldest remaining item. Transfer is performed only when it is empty, so newer items never pass older ones. Each item is moved at most once.
checks.workedTrace: Enqueue 4 and 9 into the incoming stack. The first Dequeue moves them to the outgoing stack and removes 4. Enqueue 2 without moving the still-pending 9. The next Dequeue removes 9; only then does transferring the incoming stack expose 2. The returned values are 4, 9 and 2 in FIFO order. JSON supplies [operationNames,argumentLists] for one fresh QueueTwoStacks. Void operations display null; Dequeue displays the returned item or {"error":"empty"}.

checks.spaceDerivation: O(q) persistent space: each of q queued occurrences lives in exactly one of the two stacks.

checks.actualAlgorithm: Set ways[0]=1. Process denominations one at a time, adding ways[a-coin] into ways[a] for increasing amounts.
checks.correctness: After processing a denomination prefix, ways[a] counts exactly combinations using that prefix. Increasing amounts permits repeated use of the current coin; processing each coin once avoids counting orderings.
checks.workedTrace: For amount 8 and denominations [2,3,5], the three unordered combinations are 2+2+2+2, 2+3+3, and 3+5. Processing each denomination in the outer loop adds each combination once; 5+3 is the same combination as 3+5, not a fourth answer.
checks.edgeCases: Zero target no denominations unreachable target coins larger than target. Amount zero has one combination (choose no coins), even with no denominations. Positive amount with no usable coins has zero combinations.
checks.timeDerivation: O(A*d+A+d+1) time for amount A and d denominations: initialize A+1 cells, then visit up to A cells per denomination. This also covers empty denominations and amount zero.
checks.spaceDerivation: O(A+1) auxiliary space: one count per subtotal from 0 through A.
checks.callableAgreement: public int ChangePossibilitiesBottomUp(int amount, int[] denominations) Arguments follow the displayed callable signature; the returned value is serialized directly. Preserve supplied arrays and object structure as stated in the problem.

checks.actualAlgorithm: Reject source outcomes 6 and 7; return every remaining outcome unchanged.
checks.correctness: Each accepted source value has the same probability 1/7. Conditioning on acceptance gives probability 1/5 for each result; repeated independent attempts preserve that distribution.
checks.workedTrace: With injected draws 6, 7, 3, reject 6 and 7 and return 3. In general each accepted source value 1..5 has the same source probability, so conditioning on acceptance gives probability 1/5. The judge output true denotes passed range, source-use and probability properties, not a fixed rolled value. Rand5 has no value arguments and returns one integer 1..5. JSON contains a judge-only forced Rand7 draw prefix; expected true denotes random-source/range/distribution checks, not the rolled integer.
checks.edgeCases: Repeated rejections every accepted value do not map rejected outcomes modulo five. Any number of 6/7 draws must be rejected; returning draw modulo five would bias outcomes. Every call uses fresh supplied randomness.
checks.timeDerivation: Expected O(1) time: each attempt succeeds with probability 5/7, so the expected number of source calls is 7/5. There is no finite worst-case call bound.
checks.spaceDerivation: O(1) auxiliary space: retain only the current draw, regardless of the number of rejected attempts.

checks.actualAlgorithm: First detect an unbounded zero-weight type. Otherwise compute the best value for each capacity by considering the last positive-weight item selected.

Two weight-5 items yield only 26; three weight-3 items yield 21. The unbounded dynamic program reuses earlier capacity optima to find 27.

Joining the first list's tail to the second list's head places all smaller nodes before all remaining nodes and contains every original node exactly once. Empty sides are handled by returning the other head.

checks.actualAlgorithm: Floyd collision detection, then reset one pointer to the head and advance both equally to the entry.
checks.correctness: If the fast pointer or its next link reaches null, there is no cycle. Otherwise let the noncyclic prefix have length mu and the cycle length lambda. At collision, slow has traveled t steps and fast 2t, so t is a multiple of lambda. The collision's cycle offset is therefore -mu modulo lambda. A pointer reset to the head reaches the entry after mu steps, while the other advances from that offset by mu and also reaches the entry. Before that point the reset pointer lies in the noncyclic prefix, so this is their first meeting. No field is written.
checks.workedTrace: For values [6,1,6,4,8] and cycleIndex=2, the tail returns to the original second 6 node. With prefix length 2 and cycle length 3, the pointers first collide inside the cycle. Reset one to index 0 and take equal steps; after two steps both reach original index 2. Return that original object, despite the equal-valued head.
checks.edgeCases: Empty and acyclic lists return null. Self-loop, cycle at the head, and a long prefix before a short cycle. Repeated payloads must not be mistaken for repeated node identities.

checks.actualAlgorithm: Three disjoint fixed array intervals with separate sizes.
checks.correctness: For each stack s, its occupied prefix of its reserved interval contains exactly its current bottom-to-top sequence, and size[s] is its length. Push writes at the next free offset and increases only that size. Pop reads the last occupied offset and decreases only that size; Peek reads without changing it. The intervals are disjoint, so these changes cannot affect another stack. Checks occur before writes, preserving state on every error.
checks.workedTrace: With capacity 2, push 8 then 3 onto stack 0 and push 7 onto stack 2. Stack 0 is full and its Peek returns 3; stack 2's Peek returns 7. Popping stack 0 returns 3 and leaves 8 at its top. A push to a full stack fails even if stack 1 is empty, because this variant reserves fixed slots.

checks.actualAlgorithm: Clear an inclusive interval with a width mask, then OR the fitting replacement shifted to low.
checks.correctness: The mask has ones exactly at the interval positions. AND with its complement keeps every outside bit and clears every inside bit. The fitting insertion has no bits beyond that interval after shifting. OR therefore sets each inside bit to the corresponding insertion bit and cannot affect an outside bit. The signed conversion changes only the numerical interpretation, not the 32-bit pattern.
checks.workedTrace: For word 240 (binary 11110000), insert 5 (101), low 1 and high 3, clearing positions 1..3 leaves 11110000. Aligning 101 yields 00001010. OR produces 11111010, or 250. Inserting zero into those positions would clear them rather than preserving old ones.
checks.edgeCases: Full-width replacement, including a negative insertion. A one-bit interval at position zero or 31. Zero insertion clears old one bits; unrelated bits remain set.
checks.timeDerivation: O(1) time for a fixed 32-bit word: a constant number of masks, shifts and bitwise operations.
checks.spaceDerivation: O(1) auxiliary space.

checks.actualAlgorithm: Emit at most 31 digits by exact doubling and subtracting each units bit.
checks.correctness: After emitting k digits, the original value equals their fractional value plus the current remainder divided by 2^k. Doubling and subtracting the emitted units digit preserves this invariant, with remainder in [0,1). These operations are exact for the admitted binary64 values: doubling shifts the exponent, and subtracting one from a value in [1,2) loses no fractional information. Zero remainder gives the exact value with no trailing zeros. If the remainder is nonzero after 31 steps, at least another digit is necessary, so ERROR is required.

checks.correctness: Before recording each window length, remove leftmost bits until the window contains at most one zero. Its left boundary is the earliest boundary that makes this window valid: an earlier discarded boundary would retain two zeros. Thus it is the longest valid interval ending at that right boundary. Every obtainable run is such a valid interval and has some right endpoint, so taking the maximum over all 32 endpoints gives exactly the best run. Negative numbers are read through their fixed 32-bit patterns, with logical bit extraction.

The sliding window discards enough of the first run when the second zero arrives, rather than allowing both zeros to be flipped.

checks.actualAlgorithm: Intersect endpoint masks per affected byte and OR them into the original packed buffer.

checks.actualAlgorithm: Iterate the three-term last-hop recurrence while retaining only the three preceding counts.
checks.correctness: Let W(n) be the required count, with W(0)=1 and W(n)=0 for n<0. Removing a route's last hop gives exactly one route counted by W(n-1), W(n-2) or W(n-3), and appending that hop reverses the mapping. Thus W(n) is their sum with no overlap or omission. Before each loop iteration, the three stored counts represent precisely those three preceding arguments. Updating them after the sum preserves the invariant and returns W(steps). Negative inputs are rejected before iteration.
checks.workedTrace: For four stairs, the counts W(0)..W(4) are 1,1,2,4,7. The final value is W(3)+W(2)+W(1)=4+2+1. For example [1,3] and [3,1] are distinct routes; treating hop sizes as an unordered coin combination would undercount.
checks.edgeCases: Negative signed endpoint, zero and one stair. Three-hop routes must not be confused with two-hop stair problems. The largest admitted steps value, 36, still fits the signed result type.
checks.timeDerivation: O(steps) time for nonnegative steps, with constant time for negative inputs.
checks.spaceDerivation: O(1) auxiliary space: three preceding counts and a temporary sum.
checks.callableAgreement: Signed int bounds are justified by the explicit domains and executed endpoints. Arrays are zero-initialized, ways[0] is set before the denomination passes, and recursive multiplication uses ordinary method self-calls without hidden helper state. Collection outputs use concrete Lists. Local recursive functions copy char buffers into immutable strings; the set grader canonicalizes member/outer ordering and rejects boolean or oversized integer members without an exception. checks.correctness: Initially the result contains precisely the empty set, all subsets of zero processed members. Inductively, existing subsets are exactly the subsets that exclude the next distinct member. Appending that member to a copy of each old subset gives exactly those that include it. The groups are disjoint, and the copy mapping is one-to-one, so no subset is omitted or repeated. Copying before appending preserves the old subsets and the original input.

checks.actualAlgorithm: Denomination-first one-dimensional combination DP, increasing amounts within each denomination pass.
checks.correctness: Before processing a coin c, ways[a] counts combinations of a using only earlier denominations. During the increasing amount pass, the old ways[a] counts combinations using no c, while ways[a-c] already counts combinations using earlier coins and any number of c. checks.actualAlgorithm: Sort auxiliary indices by width; compute the best height with each indexed box as bottom by checking all earlier strictly smaller boxes.
checks.correctness: Process boxes by increasing width. Any box that can sit above the current box has smaller width and was processed earlier. By induction its stored value is the best stack with that box at the bottom. Taking the maximum over all earlier boxes strictly smaller in width, height and depth therefore finds the best possible top stack for the current bottom. Adding the current height yields its optimal total. Every nonempty feasible stack has some bottom box, so the maximum stored value is globally optimal. Strict decreases prevent reuse or cycles, and the original input is never reordered.
checks.workedTrace: For [[5,5,5],[4,3,4],[3,2,3],[6,1,6]], the first three boxes form a stack of height 5+3+2=10. The last box is wider and deeper but only height 1, so it cannot serve as the bottom beneath those taller boxes. Sorting by width provides a processing order, not a greedy choice of the answer.
checks.edgeCases: Empty input, one box and identical boxes. Equality in any one dimension prevents stacking. A tall narrow box versus a wide short box; shuffled input and a full strict chain.

checks.edgeCases: No people, same-year lifetimes, duplicate date rows. Birth coinciding with another death; earliest tied year and the 2000 endpoint.

checks.spaceDerivation: O(Y) change counters including a death-after-2000 sentinel; Y is fixed at 101.

checks.actualAlgorithm: Iterative fixed-width XOR sum and shifted-AND carries.
checks.correctness: For each bit position, XOR contributes the low sum bit and the shifted AND contributes its carry into the next position. Replacing the operands by those two patterns preserves their total modulo 2^32. Each pending carry moves left, so after at most 32 rounds none remains within the word. The remaining pattern is therefore the required modular sum. C#/Java/JavaScript naturally observe the fixed-width pattern; Python masks each carry and reinterprets the final sign. C++ uses unsigned shifts and a fixed-width byte copy for the signed result, avoiding undefined signed left shift or narrowing.
checks.workedTrace: For 5 and 3, the first XOR is 6 and the pending carry is 2. Next they become 4 and 4, then 0 and 8, then 8 and 0. The returned result is 8. For -1 and 1, the carry propagates through the whole word and is discarded above bit 31, leaving zero.
checks.edgeCases: Zero, equal values, negative values and long carry chains. Both signed endpoints and sums that wrap across either endpoint.
checks.timeDerivation: O(w) bit-operation rounds for a w-bit word, at most 32 here; therefore bounded O(1) for this fixed-width callable.
checks.spaceDerivation: O(1) auxiliary scalar storage; iterative implementations use no recursion stack.
checks.callableAgreement: Read all five bodies and operation restrictions: no arithmetic operator or arithmetic helper is used. C#/C++ shift unsigned 32-bit patterns; C++17 memcpy into int32_t reinterprets the final bits without signed overflow. Java/JS use native 32-bit bitwise operations. Python masks operands/carry and reconstructs the signed result using complement. Long carry chains, both signed endpoints and wrapping sums are executed against independent modular mathematical addition. Read exact bodies: AddWithoutArithmetic uses unsigned carry shifts and explicit unchecked signed conversions. CountDigitTwos uses long before multiplying place blocks. Array-return expressions match int[]; bounded sums and candidate products stay within int. All arrays supplied to algorithms remain unchanged.

If digit=2, that run includes low+1 numbers; if digit>2, it includes all p. Thus the formula counts precisely all occurrences at that position among 0..n. Summing over positions counts every occurrence once, including both positions in 22. Higher leading positions contribute nothing. Wide intermediates prevent overflow of 10p at the billions place.

The zero-k branch returns before accessing a heap root.

checks.actualAlgorithm: Cache canonical sorted-letter keys, order decorated occurrences, and write words back into the original array.

Decoration retains one entry for each original occurrence, and writing every decorated word back preserves the complete multiset and length. Returned values mirror that final array. Ordering inside an equal-key group is irrelevant to the contract.

This preserves every possible target occurrence in the remaining interval. Every iteration shrinks the interval, and returning -1 after it empties therefore means the target is absent. A returned index is checked directly.

checks.actualAlgorithm: Iterative unbalanced BST with left-subtree occurrence counts; equal inserts go left.
checks.correctness: Every insertion preserves the BST rule left<=node<right and increments a node's left count exactly when the new occurrence enters that left subtree. During a query, the accumulated count contains exactly the smaller/equal occurrences already skipped on right turns. At equality, every left-subtree occurrence is <=value, and the current node is the one excluded occurrence, so accumulated+leftCount is the required rank. If traversal reaches no matching node, the value is absent and -1 is returned regardless of the partial accumulated count. Iterative traversal avoids recursion-depth failures on a skewed stream.

checks.actualAlgorithm: Build one normalized-word frequency dictionary and answer a batch of lookups.
checks.correctness: After processing any prefix of book, the dictionary count for each normalized word equals its occurrences in that prefix: inserting a new normalized key starts its count and every later occurrence increments it once. Induction gives exact counts for the entire book. A normalized query identifies precisely its case-insensitive equivalence class; lookup returns that count, or zero when no occurrence created its key. Appending answers in query order preserves repeated queries and their positions.
checks.workedTrace: For book=[Red,blue,RED,green] and queries=[red,BLUE,missing,Red], normalized counts are red:2, blue:1, green:1. The answers are [2,1,0,2]. Red and RED contribute to the same count; the repeated red query does not consume a book occurrence.
checks.edgeCases: Empty book or query array; all queries absent. Mixed case, repeated book words and repeated queries.
checks.timeDerivation: Expected O(B+Q) character work for B book characters and Q query characters, assuming expected constant dictionary access per bounded-length key. Hash-table collisions can worsen this bound.
checks.spaceDerivation: O(D*L+q) storage for D distinct normalized book words of maximum length L and q returned counts; query normalization uses O(L) temporary storage.
checks.callableAgreement: Read all five actual bodies. Invariant token keys and private array clones preserve contracts.

checks.actualAlgorithm: Count Parent depths, align the deeper node, then advance original references together to their first meeting.
checks.correctness: Advancing only the deeper pointer cannot skip the common ancestor: every ancestor of the shallower node has depth no greater than that node. After alignment, both pointers are at the same depth. Moving them together preserves this equality and visits ancestors in decreasing depth order. A meeting is therefore common to both original paths, and any deeper common ancestor would have caused an earlier meeting. If their roots differ, they remain distinct until both become null, giving the required absence result. An explicit null-input check prevents treating a nonnull node as an ancestor of null.
checks.workedTrace: In rows [[9,1,2],[9,3,-1],[9,-1,-1],[9,-1,-1]], selecting first node 3 and second node 2 first aligns node 3 upward to node 1. Moving node 1 and node 2 upward together meets at original node 0. All Data values are 9, so value equality cannot solve the identity question.

checks.actualAlgorithm: Sort private original-person indices, compute strict two-dimension longest-ending lengths and reconstruct predecessor indices.
checks.correctness: Every predecessor of a person in a valid top-to-bottom tower has smaller height and therefore occurs earlier in the private sorted order. For each person, the recurrence takes one plus the largest valid predecessor tower length, or one if none exists. Induction over that order proves each recorded length is optimal among towers ending there. The global best endpoint consequently has maximum possible length. Following its recorded predecessor links reconstructs only strict height/weight links, and reversing them yields top-to-bottom original indices. Private index sorting leaves caller rows unchanged.
checks.workedTrace: For people=[[65,100],[70,150],[56,90]], the sorted index order is [2,0,1]. Each person can follow the previous one, so return [2,0,1]. For [[60,100],[60,90]], only one person can be used despite the different weights, because heights must also increase strictly.
checks.edgeCases: Empty/single person, duplicate rows and ties in either dimension. A best tower using neither original input order nor every person; arbitrary maximum-tower ties.

checks.actualAlgorithm: Prefix minimum-unknown-cost DP with saved predecessor positions reconstructs actual tokens.
checks.correctness: Every produced tokenization ends in either a recognized word or an unrecognized segment. The latter can be split into single unknown characters without changing its cost, so the recurrence considering one unknown character is sufficient. Removing the final recognized word or unknown character leaves a strictly shorter prefix with optimal cost by induction. Taking the minimum over these possibilities therefore gives the global minimum. Saved predecessor positions strictly decrease during reconstruction and concatenate to the complete original text, proving both valid coverage and minimum cost.

Testing all four endpoints for exact membership in both segments therefore finds an intersection whenever one exists. If no endpoint passes, the parallel/degenerate segments are disjoint. Readonly inputs are never reordered.

checks.actualAlgorithm: Complete 2^31-bit bitmap for one-pass full memory, or 2048 distinct-value block counters followed by a 2^20-bit bitmap and one rewind.
checks.correctness: In full mode, processing v sets exactly its presence bit and never clears a bit. After the pass, a zero bit is therefore equivalent to absence; fewer than 2^31 file entries guarantees one exists. In small mode, every integer belongs to exactly one of 2048 blocks. Since values are distinct, each count equals the number of present values in that block. At least one count is below its capacity, so the selected block contains an absent value. On the second pass only values whose high block bits match the chosen block set local presence bits. A zero local bit therefore denotes a truly absent domain value. The block-index comparison avoids overflowing an exclusive upper endpoint for the highest block. Neither proof applies to a repeated-value bucket count without the distinctness promise.
checks.workedTrace: A file represented by [[0,2],[4,4]] streams 0,1,2,4. Full mode sets those four bits and finds missing 3. In small mode block 0 has count 4<1048576; after Reset, its local bitmap again identifies 3. If [[0,1048575]] is the whole file, block 0 is full, so the small-memory search chooses block 1 and returns 1048576. A file containing 2147483647 must not overflow its stream cursor or last bitmap index.
checks.edgeCases: Empty file, duplicate values in full mode and arbitrary file order. All values of the first block present, a missing interior value, and maximum signed value present. No integer overflow at 2^31, sticky EOF, one rewind and the distinctness-only count proof.
checks.timeDerivation: Full mode O(N+U/8) worst-case byte scanning plus fixed eight-bit inspection per nonfull byte; small mode O(N+B+R/8), where U=2^31, B=2048 and R=2^20. The file is streamed once or twice, not expanded into a local array.
checks.spaceDerivation: Full mode exactly U/8=268435456 bitmap bytes plus O(1) state. Small mode 131072 bitmap bytes plus 2048 counters and O(1) state; even language object overhead for the counters stays well below 10 MiB. Supplied stream storage is excluded.
checks.callableAgreement: Read all five actual bodies and the private lazy NumberFile API. The callable never receives fixture ranges as arrays, only streamed individual integers. Full mode uses exactly 268435456 bitmap bytes and handles duplicates idempotently. Small mode uses a 131072-byte bitmap and 2048 counters; the explicit distinctness promise is essential to the count proof and is not applied to duplicate full-mode files. Java byte comparisons cast 255 to signed byte while bit tests inspect only low eight bits; C++ unsigned char, C# byte, JS Uint8Array/Uint32Array and Python bytearray have their actual bounded storage. Python counter object overhead remains well below 10 MiB. Block membership uses shifted block ID, avoiding overflow of a final exclusive 2^31 endpoint. Private stream cursors/read counts are widened before inclusive int.MaxValue increments. Independent interval-union oracle never expands the file and accepts any absent result. Cases execute both memory modes, full first blocks, repeated full-mode ranges and signed-maximum input. Five compiled negative programs reject excess EOF reads, second low-memory rewind and full-memory rewind. Tests do not claim execution of a multi-billion-entry file or runtime enforcement of arbitrary user heap allocation; source review establishes the reference memory bounds, while read/rewind limits are enforced. checks.actualAlgorithm: Iterative rejection of states 21..24 from two independent five-way draws, then reduction modulo seven.
checks.correctness: Every ordered draw pair has probability 1/25. In an accepted attempt, each result r in 0..6 has exactly the three preimages r,r+7,r+14, so its unconditional probability in that attempt is 3/25. The attempt rejects with probability 4/25, independent of earlier attempts. Thus eventual probability of each result is sum over k>=0 of (4/25)^k*(3/25)=1/7. Repeating independent source draws gives independent completed calls without retained algorithm state. Acceptance probability 21/25 implies almost-sure termination and expected 25/21 attempts; the worst-case number of attempts is unbounded.
checks.workedTrace: For source prefix [4,4,0,0], the first pair encodes 24 and is rejected. The next pair encodes 0 and returns 0. Accepted states 2,9,16 all return 2, giving it exactly three equally likely accepted preimages. Returning 24%7 without rejection would give output 3 an extra preimage and bias the distribution.
checks.edgeCases: Every accepted residue, rejection states 21..24 and repeated rejections. Zero-based source/result bounds and repeated independent calls. Alternative valid rejection schemes must not be rejected solely for using three draws per attempt or a larger rejected mass.
checks.timeDerivation: Expected O(1) time: 25/21 attempts and 50/21 primitive calls. Worst-case running time is unbounded because any finite run of rejections has positive probability.

checks.actualAlgorithm: Backward Fisher-Yates exchanges uniformly selected remaining occurrences into a finalized suffix.
checks.correctness: Before processing i, the suffix i+1..n-1 is final and the prefix contains exactly the remaining occurrences. Each remaining occurrence is equally likely to fill position i because its index is selected with probability 1/(i+1). The swap removes that occurrence from later choices while preserving the multiset. For any target occurrence permutation, the conditional choices needed to build it have probability 1/n,1/(n-1),...,1/2, whose product is 1/n!. Independent primitive calls and no retained cross-call state give independent shuffles. Equal-valued occurrences do not change this reasoning.
checks.workedTrace: For [10,20,30], suppose GetRandom(0,2) returns 0: swap positions 2 and 0 to obtain [30,20,10]. Then GetRandom(0,1) returns 1, so the self-swap leaves [30,20,10]. That outcome has probability 1/3*1/2=1/6, as does each of the six occurrence permutations. Skipping self-swaps as possible choices would bias the result.
checks.edgeCases: Empty/singleton arrays, duplicate occurrences and all-equal arrays. Inclusive random bounds, self-swaps, signed endpoints and 1000 elements. Repeated calls must use fresh independent choices.
checks.timeDerivation: O(n) time and exactly max(0,n-1) primitive draws for this implementation.

checks.actualAlgorithm: Reservoir sampling with one uniform slot choice for each later occurrence, leaving the original array unchanged.
checks.correctness: Initially the only count-subset of the first count occurrences is present. Assume the reservoir is uniform over count-subsets of i processed occurrences. For a target subset not containing the new occurrence, its previous reservoir survives with probability (i+1-count)/(i+1). For a target containing the new occurrence, there are i-count+1 possible prior extra members; each corresponding prior reservoir has probability 1/C(i,count), and the draw replaces that particular member with probability 1/(i+1). Both cases give 1/C(i+1,count). Induction proves a uniform final occurrence subset, including duplicates by their original indices. The original array is only read. Zero count is handled before scanning, and the returned reservoir order need not be uniform.
checks.workedTrace: For [10,20,30,40] and count=2, start with reservoir [10,20]. At i=2 a draw of 1 replaces 20 with 30, giving [10,30]. At i=3 a draw of 3 keeps the reservoir. For [7,7,9] and count=1, value 7 must occur with probability 2/3, because it has two source occurrences; selecting distinct values with probability 1/2 each would be biased.
